offences.quote: Students who submit work generated by AI, but pass it oﬀ as their own, will have committed academic misconduct.
submitting any assessment which contains work which has been generated by Artiﬁcial Intelligence. AI tools must only be used when the assessment instructions permit its use.
Generative AI tools re-present information developed by others in novel ways and so there is the risk of plagiarised content being submitted by a user as their own (which is also plagiarism)

Despite the beneﬁts of generative AI in personalised learning, assignments, and assessments, its implementation raises concerns regarding academic misconduct, including plagiarism, cheating, and contract cheating.
Staﬀ and students may not upload any content access through University-subscribed resources, including Library resources, to LLMs as this will potentially breach licence and copyright restrictions.

detection.quote: Avoid a blanket reliance on AI detection tools, as they are (currently) highly inaccurate and underscore the biases inherent in them.
Periodically reviewing students’ work to ensure criticality of their writing and to develop familiarity with their style.
